sections.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
sections.abstract: The authors introduce AMP1, a generalist model-in-the-loop robot manipulation harness, and report strong zero-shot benchmark and real-robot results against specialist policies.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper presents AMP1, a shared harness for direct model control across robot embodiments; the authors report 85.6% zero-shot success on RoboLab-120 and success in 104 of 108 real-world trials.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors say the approach is slow because the robot waits for model reasoning and cannot revise an executing trajectory; evaluations mainly use quasi-static scenes, so it is not yet suitable for mission-critical deployment.

sections.title: Test-Time Compute Scales Better with Parallel Agent Teams
sections.abstract: The paper proposes sampling many small collaborating agent teams in parallel and keeping the best verifier-scored team's result, reporting gains over independent agents and one large team on long-horizon tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report that, with a 27B model and a budget of 100 agents, teams of ten beat parallel individual agents on 10 of 12 tasks and beat a single 100-agent team on all four tasks tested at that size.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes small run pools (10–11 runs per task), only one to five runs for larger-team sizes, and use of one agent harness; without a verifier, selecting the best team becomes an additional problem.

sections.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
sections.abstract: Video-Coder trains an agent to write and execute code for a structured 3D draft video that guides a downstream video generator, using supervised fine-tuning and harness-native reinforcement learning.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors combine two curated datasets, a code-execution/3D-rendering harness, and reinforcement learning with execution and video rewards; they report gains of about 7 points on PhyGenBench and 24 points on VBench-2.0 over Minimax-H3.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence is on PhyGenBench and VBench-2.0; transfer to other video generators or real-world production use is not established by these evaluations.

sections.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
sections.abstract: CPU-ARC converts LLM reasoning traces into reusable CPU-executable caches that apply prior solutions to new, related problem instances with less model inference.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper introduces reusable semantic-function caches built from reasoning traces; across eight math/science benchmarks, it reports invocation costs 16–291 times lower than the source model, with cache construction costing 12–84 times a source invocation.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors target repetitive tasks whose reasoning transfers across varied inputs; the up-front construction cost must be amortized, and novel or unmatched requests still need a full-model fallback.

sections.title: Knowing When to Intervene: Causal Evaluation of AI Agents
sections.abstract: The authors develop a framework using randomized interventions within agent trajectories to estimate how review or steering policies affect final outcomes, with effects varying by action and state in three benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The paper uses sequential randomization, AIPW, and structural nested mean models to estimate intervention effects, and reports heterogeneous effects on tau-bench Retail, ToolSandbox, and ImpossibleBench.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that estimates for some target policies rely on correctly specified structural nested mean models; experiments cover relatively small models and established benchmarks, which may be saturated by frontier systems.

sections.title: Computer-Use Agents Are Embodied Generalists
sections.abstract: The authors frame embodied tasks as software interaction and report that one computer-use agent design, without task-specific tuning, placed in four ECCV workshop competitions across navigation and visual tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that computer-use agents can transfer visual grounding and exploration skills to embodied tasks through a shared screen-and-controls interface, and report results across four competition tracks.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors' text-action experiment covers a two-arm simulated setup; they note higher-degree-of-freedom robots may need more efficient action representations, and real-time control remains a separate challenge.
